What changed, and why

The repository began empty. It now includes content-based PDF/image decoding, bounded in-memory uploads, staff geometry and glyph recognition, diatonic pitch mapping, key and accidental scope, rhythm estimation, a responsive review interface, and sampled piano playback. Each staff is a separate practice phrase so unrelated exercises are easy to select.

Image reading is imperfect. The app shows note markers, explicit scope warnings, heuristic reading indicators, and controls to correct notes, rests, lengths, clef, and key. MIDI and rendered WAV exports reflect those corrections, tempo, and transposition.

The audio scheduler uses the Web Audio clock, with cancellation tokens and short release fades. Regression fixes cover isolated flags near slurs, symbol/beam confusion, staff-switch seek state, stale audition highlights, keyboard upload, and accessible secondary text.

Run it locally

From the project folder, run .\start.ps1, or install requirements.txt in a Python virtual environment and run python app.py. Open http://127.0.0.1:8765. The server binds only to loopback. Initial dependency installation uses the network; score processing and piano playback use local files thereafter.

Verification evidence

  • Recognition — Per-agent run: 13 synthetic end-to-end tests passed, including independently specified demo pitches/rhythm, both clefs, key/accidental scope, flagged notes under slurs, beams, dots, rests, resizing and low-contrast JPEG.
  • HTTP and file handling — Per-agent run: 26 tests passed for real PNG/alpha/EXIF/PDF decoding, encryption, invalid pages, malformed files/forms, bounded chunked uploads, origin/host policy and in-memory spooling.
  • Piano and notation editing — Per-agent runs: 15 audio and 39 notation tests passed. Fake audio-clock lifecycle, exact MIDI/WAV structure, all 15 keys in both clefs, roundtrips, explicit/inherited naturals, manual edits and bounds.

Six supplied PDF pages were evaluated locally. The independent reviewer checked complete phrases and accidental/rhythm passages against rendered source notation. Private source pages and event-level extracts are excluded from this report and Git.

Actual browser MP3 decoding, transport and downloads were exercised. A rendered edited D4 phrase produced stereo 44.1 kHz 16-bit PCM, 5.16 seconds, nonzero RMS 0.00806 and a strongest FFT bin near 293 Hz, consistent with D4. The MIDI download has a format-0 header and 480 ticks per quarter note. Device speaker listening was not independently measured.

Real local-server checks covered desktop and 390-pixel mobile viewports, note/rest corrections, MIDI/WAV downloads, play/pause/resume, keyboard PDF upload and six-page selection. The narrow layout measured document clientWidth=375 and scrollWidth=375. English is the only implemented language. Final integrated recheck is pending.

Independent assessment

The separate reviewer defined the rubric before final assessment and reported failures for correction. Scores describe the documented clean printed monophonic scope and the evidence inspected; they are not an accuracy guarantee for arbitrary music.

DimensionScoreEvidence and basis

Remaining limits

  • Recognition is an editable heuristic draft for clean, level, printed monophonic treble/bass staves. High reading confidence does not guarantee transcription accuracy.
  • Handwriting, perspective photos, dense/chordal notation, multiple voices, ties, tuplets, repeats, grace notes and expressive performance are not reliably interpreted. Phrase slurs are ignored; ties require manual consolidation.
  • Staves play independently; the app does not infer multi-staff instrument parts or join systems. A key signature alone does not determine major versus minor mode.
  • Uploads are bounded to 25 MiB and raster images to 30 megapixels; processed images have a 2,600-pixel long-edge limit. Local process/browser memory and operating-system swap remain outside application storage controls.
  • Audio needs a browser gesture and can be suspended by background/locked-device policies. WAV is limited to ten minutes; transport is limited to thirty minutes and 20,000 events.
  • The server is intended for loopback use. It has no public-hosting authentication or deployment hardening. Initial dependency installation needs internet access.
  • Final independent acceptance and full integrated checks are pending in this draft report.
